read.sections.0.text.source: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. Environments change over time. As the climate changes, some places now get heavier rain, while others have longer dry seasons. People change places too. For example, when many trees are cut down on a hillside, heavy rain can wash the soil away more easily, because there are no roots to hold it. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes covers the low footbridge. Children use the bridge to reach school, and traders use it to reach the market. The community needs a plan.
read.sections.0.text.back: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. The environment changes over time. When the climate changes, some places now have heavier rain, while other places have longer dry seasons. People also change places. For example, when many trees on a hillside are cut down, heavy rain more easily washes the soil away, because there are no longer roots holding the soil. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes makes water cover the low footbridge. Children use the bridge to get to school, and traders use the bridge to get to the market. The community needs a plan.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: The environment is everything around us. It is land, water, air, plants and animals. The environment can change. Some places now have more rain. read.sections.1.text.note: 'Vành đai Xanh Vĩ đại' for Great Green Wall (Vietnamese name varies); 'cây ngập mặn' for mangrove trees; 'cây thủy sinh' for water plants; Senegal, Djibouti, Bangladesh spellings. Check each.
read.sections.1.text.source: Around the world, communities adapt to changes in their environment. In Bangladesh, many fields stay under water for months in the rainy season. Some farmers build floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on top. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are working on the Great Green Wall. They plant trees and care for the land to stop it from turning into desert. On many coasts in Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the shore from waves. Each of these is a response that fits the local place.
read.sections.1.text.back: Around the world, communities adapt to changes in the environment. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water for many months in the rainy season. Some farmers make floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on top. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are carrying out the Great Green Wall project. They plant trees and care for the soil to stop the land turning into desert. On many coasts of Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the coast from waves. Each of these is a way of responding that suits the place where one lives.

read.sections.1.simpler.note: Great Green Wall is described, not named, as in the English. Check 'cây ven biển' is clear.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: Communities around the world adapt. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water in the rainy season. So some farmers make gardens that float. They grow vegetables on top. In Africa, many countries plant trees across a wide, dry area. The trees help stop the land from turning into desert. In parts of Asia, people plant trees by the sea. The roots help keep the land safe from waves. Each response fits its place.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Communities around the world adapt. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water in the rainy season. So some farmers make floating gardens. They grow vegetables on top. In Africa, many countries plant trees across a wide, dry area. The trees help stop the land turning into desert. In some places in Asia, people plant trees by the sea. The tree roots help keep the coast safe from waves. Each way of responding suits its place.

read.sections.2.text.note: 'dữ liệu di động' for 'data'; 'sự hòa nhập' for 'inclusion'; 'biển báo' for sign (kept different from 'cảnh báo' for alert). | Review: Cart pushed by hand: 'xe đẩy' avoids reading as a truck. Native to confirm. [Reviewer changed: xe hàng → xe đẩy]
read.sections.2.text.source: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A warning sign is quick, but it does not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read it. Raising the bridge lowers the risk, and a ramp helps people who use wheelchairs or push carts. Phone alerts can warn people early, but not everyone has a phone or data. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure that everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often, two ideas together work better than one, and it helps to ask the people who use the bridge.
read.sections.2.text.back: A way of responding works only if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A sign is fast, but it does not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read the sign. Raising the bridge reduces the danger, and the slope helps people who use wheelchairs or push carts. A phone warning can tell everyone early, but not everyone has a phone or mobile data. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often two ideas combined are better than one, and you should ask the very people who use the bridge.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: A plan only works if people can use it. A sign is quick. But it does not make the bridge safe. A higher bridge is safer. A ramp helps people who cannot use steps. A phone alert warns people early. But not everyone has a phone. Paper notices at the market help too. When everyone can use a plan, that is called inclusion. Two ideas together can work better than one.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: A plan works only if people can use it. A sign is fast. But a sign does not make the bridge safe. A higher bridge is safer. A slope helps people who cannot go on steps. A phone warning tells everyone early. But not everyone has a phone. Printed notices at the market help too. When everyone can use a plan, this is called inclusion. Two ideas together can be better than one idea.

Also 'rào cản', 'hòa nhập'.
watch.summary.source: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that work for all, a safe path for all, and safe places that all can use. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
watch.summary.back: In this short video from UNICEF, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger arrives. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video calls for warnings that everyone can use, a safe path for everyone, and safe places that everyone can use. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
